label: Rhythmic augmentation
learning_takeaway: Recognize a motive whose durations expand proportionally while its pitch pattern remains recognizable.
support_note: Section describes exact rhythmic doubling as the usual case.

label: Musical diminution
learning_takeaway: Distinguish proportional rhythmic shortening from changing only some durations.
support_note: Definition contrasts halving with more general shorter rhythmic values.

label: Melodic retrograde
learning_takeaway: Hear how reversing note order differs from inverting intervals.
support_note: Section identifies exact reverse order with a Toxic example.

label: Melodic inversion
learning_takeaway: Distinguish interval-preserving real inversion from key-preserving tonal inversion.
support_note: Bach example and explicit real-versus-tonal distinction support the control.

label: Appoggiatura
learning_takeaway: Follow an expressive non-chord note approached by leap and resolved by step.
support_note: Both upward and downward resolutions are explicitly permitted.

label: Pedal point
learning_takeaway: Hear a held note change harmonic status while surrounding chords move.
support_note: A chord tone becomes a non-chord tone as harmony changes.

label: Suspension in tonal music
learning_takeaway: Trace preparation, accented dissonance and downward stepwise resolution.
support_note: Definition distinguishes held-over preparation and resolution from other ornaments.

label: Cadential six-four chord
learning_takeaway: Understand why an inverted tonic sonority can perform a dominant function.
support_note: The textbook explicitly assigns dominant function before the following V chord.

label: Additive minimalism
locator: 35.1 Two Pages and Einstein on the Beach examples
learning_takeaway: Track growth by gradually extending repeated musical patterns.
support_note: The examples add patterned repetitions or duration rather than new themes.

label: Musical phase shifting
learning_takeaway: Compare gradual desynchronization with discrete shifts of a repeated pattern.
support_note: Piano Phase speeds one part; Clapping Music jumps between rotations.

label: Tonal answer in fugue
learning_takeaway: Understand why a fugue answer alters intervals to navigate tonic and dominant.
support_note: Real answers preserve intervals; tonal answers modify them.

label: Countersubject
learning_takeaway: Identify recurring counterpoint accompanying successive subject entries.
support_note: The text contrasts a consistent countersubject with fresh accompaniment.

label: Pitch (music)
learning_takeaway: Relate perceived high and low notes to their ordering on a keyboard.
support_note: The passage describes pitches rising toward the piano keyboard's right.

label: Inharmonicity of musical strings
learning_takeaway: Explain why stiff strings have stretched modal frequencies rather than exact harmonic multiples.
support_note: Bending stiffness affects higher modes more strongly.

label: Mode locking in bowed strings
learning_takeaway: See how periodic bowing can enforce harmonic motion despite inharmonic string resonances.
support_note: The nonlinear stick-slip drive pulls resonances toward harmonic ratios.

label: String harmonic
learning_takeaway: Compare lightly touching an open string with touching a separately stopped string.
support_note: Natural uses open strings; artificial harmonics require a stopped string.

label: Sympathetic resonance
locator: Exercise for guitarists before Harmonic tuning on guitars
learning_takeaway: Understand how shared harmonics transfer vibration through a guitar bridge.
support_note: Plucking low E can drive the tuned B or high E string.

label: Clapping Music
learning_takeaway: Hear how discrete rhythmic rotations create changing alignments without a gradual tempo drift.
support_note: Reich's 1972 work switches rotation at a measure's downbeat.

label: Piano Phase
learning_takeaway: Follow two repeated patterns as one pianist gradually changes their alignment.
support_note: The twelve-note pattern and gradual speed change are described.

label: Two Pages
learning_takeaway: Explore Glass's additive process through repetitions that successively omit final notes.
support_note: The analysis describes how each additional repetition is shortened.

label: Einstein on the Beach
learning_takeaway: Observe a five-chord progression expanding through added subdivisions.
support_note: The named scene gradually lengthens each chord's allotted duration.

label: Bach's Fugue in C minor, BWV 847
learning_takeaway: Trace full subject entries alternating with development through fragmented motives.
support_note: The analyzed fugue supplies both subject exposition and an episode.

label: Bach's Invention in C major, BWV 772
learning_takeaway: Recognize inversion and rhythmic augmentation within one tightly developed keyboard work.
support_note: Figures explicitly identify both techniques in the 1723 invention.

label: Adagio for Strings
learning_takeaway: Hear how a 4–3 suspension delays resolution in Barber's work.
support_note: The named score example illustrates the previously defined suspension.

label: Neapolitan chord
learning_takeaway: Recognize the flattened-supertonic major chord as a chromatic predominant.
support_note: Text identifies flat II, common first inversion and predominant function.

label: Augmented sixth chord
learning_takeaway: Follow two chromatic voices approaching the dominant from opposite semitone directions.
support_note: Raised fourth and lowered sixth approach scale degree five.

label: Species counterpoint
learning_takeaway: Learn how controlled note ratios organize practice in combining independent melodies.
support_note: The passage enumerates one through four notes against a longer value.

label: Counterpoint
learning_takeaway: Distinguish simultaneous melodic lines from a melody with accompaniment.
support_note: The textbook explicitly contrasts contrapuntal and homophonic textures.

label: Missing fundamental
locator: Pitch, frequency, harmonics and missing fundamental
learning_takeaway: Understand why a bass pitch remains audible when a speaker omits its fundamental.
support_note: The example explains pitch from spacing between the surviving harmonics.

label: Stretch tuning
learning_takeaway: Explain slightly widened piano octaves through the inharmonicity of stiff strings.
support_note: Tuning matches an upper fundamental to a lower string's sharp second partial.

label: Tartini tone
learning_takeaway: Identify a difference tone produced by nonlinear interaction of two frequencies.
support_note: The difference-frequency component is identified as the Tartini tone.

label: Just intonation
locator: What is all the fuss about temperament?
learning_takeaway: Explore why pure small-ratio intervals create compromises when changing keys.
support_note: The source contrasts pure fifths and thirds and limits beyond the home key.

label: Meantone temperament
locator: What is all the fuss about temperament?
learning_takeaway: See how slightly narrowed fifths improve thirds but constrain modulation.
support_note: The worked tuning comparison spreads the discrepancy across four fifths.

label: Wind-instrument end correction
learning_takeaway: Understand why an open pipe resonates as though it were slightly longer.
support_note: Reflection develops beyond the geometric opening, lowering the modeled resonance.

label: Clarinet overblowing at the twelfth
learning_takeaway: Compare a clarinet's next register with a flute's octave using boundary conditions.
support_note: The approximate closed-open cylinder supports an odd-harmonic series.

label: Prepared piano
learning_takeaway: Hear how objects placed between piano strings transform its available timbres.
support_note: The Trust describes Cage's physical preparations and supervised sampled instrument.

label: Glass armonica
locator: Why does rubbing your finger around the rim of a wine glass make a note?
learning_takeaway: Connect friction-driven glass vibration with Franklin's rotating-bowl instrument.
support_note: The source describes stick-slip excitation and bowls on a rotating axle.

learning_takeaway: Explore a three-movement performance that directs attention toward ambient sound.
support_note: The official Trust description emphasizes listening and ambient performance recordings.

label: Sonatas and Interludes
learning_takeaway: Connect a particular Cage cycle with reproducible preparations altering piano sound.
support_note: The Trust identifies the 1946–48 work and sampling of its actual preparation materials.

label: Gradus ad Parnassum
learning_takeaway: Explore Fux's historical organization of contrapuntal practice into rhythmic species.
support_note: The 1725 text is explicitly named as teaching species counterpoint.
